items.problem: Validator was invoked via a bare relative path with backslashes ('& ".github\skills\...\Validate-UwpMigration.ps1"'); PowerShell parsed the leading '.github' segment as a module-qualified command, so the script never ran, yet $LASTEXITCODE stayed 0 and 'VALIDATE_EXIT=0' printed as if it had passed. An agent keying off the exit code alone would silently skip the mandatory validation gate and declare done.
items.evidence: session-log.txt turn 4, lines 4617-4623: '& : The module '.github' could not be loaded. For more information, run 'Import-Module .github'. ... VALIDATE_EXIT=0'. Recovered in turn 5 with an absolute path.
items.covered_at: SKILL.md '## Process' script list (lines 24-31) and each invocation example, which show '& "<skill-root>/scripts/X.ps1"' but never state that <skill-root> must be an ABSOLUTE path, nor warn about the relative-path module-qualified-command failure that leaves $LASTEXITCODE unchanged.
items.proposed_improvement: Add one prominent invocation rule where the four scripts are introduced in SKILL.md: resolve <skill-root> to an ABSOLUTE path (or prefix with '.\'); never invoke via a bare relative 'dir\script.ps1' because PowerShell parses the leading segment as a module-qualified command and the call fails WITHOUT setting $LASTEXITCODE, so an exit-code check falsely reads success. Confirm each script actually ran (look for its header line), not just $LASTEXITCODE.
items.generalizes: Every scenario invokes these four scripts (Initialize/Get-MigrationPattern/Test-AppLaunch/Validate) from the working directory on Windows; a relative backslash path is the natural thing an agent types, so this module-qualified-command trap — and the false-pass it produces on the mandatory validation gate — can recur in any scenario.

items.problem: CS8618 nullable warnings on the migrated SDK-sample model class (SampleConfiguration.cs 'Scenario' with non-nullable 'string Title' / 'Type ClassType' auto-properties) under the WinUI scaffold's <Nullable>enable</Nullable>. Cost the dev-agent a diagnose+fix cycle.
items.evidence: session-log.txt turns 1-3, lines 4552-4610: '4 Warning(s)' all CS8618 on SampleConfiguration.cs, fixed by adding '= string.Empty' / '= typeof(object)'.
items.covered_at: MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md '## Common build errors after the namespace rewrite' (lines 5-55) lists CS0104/CS0227/CS0101/CS0246 but not CS8618.
items.proposed_improvement: Add a short 'CS8618' subsection under 'Common build errors after the namespace rewrite' naming the cause (UWP model/config classes copied verbatim into the nullable-enabled scaffold) and the one-line fix (initialize the property, e.g. '= string.Empty' / '= null!', or make it nullable).
items.generalizes: SampleConfiguration.cs (and ControlInfoData-style model classes) with non-nullable auto-properties ship in essentially every Microsoft UWP SDK sample; migrated into the nullable-enabled WinUI scaffold they always emit CS8618, so this warning recurs across scenarios.
